hook: A redesigned HaloTag reacts only with a modified substrate, allowing two targets to be labeled in cells.
summary: OrthoTag, made by structure-guided design and directed evolution, reacts with a modified chloroalkane and ignores HaloTag's substrate, and the reverse. Purified-protein rates show 109-fold mutual orthogonality, and two-color labeling worked in mammalian cells. Tests were limited to cultured cells and a small set of labeling experiments.
title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
